findings.title: SQLi Filter Bypass via Keyword Stripping - Private Job Access + CTF Flag
findings.description: The POST /jobs endpoint takes a job_type parameter and concatenates it unsanitized into a SQL query. A server-side filter strips known SQL keywords (OR, UNION, SELECT, etc.) and blocks the value 'private' with a 403. However, by embedding a banned keyword INSIDE the word 'private', the filter removes it and reconstructs the intended value - e.g. 'privORate' strips 'OR' to yield 'private', which the 403 check never sees because the check fires AFTER keyword stripping. This allows unauthenticated access to private jobs containing the CTF flag.
